title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: choose file extensions from a curated list
summary: The rollout, licensing and existing-policy behaviour are supported. Hold for the statement that policy-editing roles are undocumented, despite published permissions, and for turning the absence of a documented picker switch into a categorical claim that it cannot be disabled.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a pre-curated picker for the Endpoint DLP file extension condition.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP now includes a pre curated list of file extensions for the file extension condition.

claims.claim: Previously, extensions were entered as free-form text and could include unsupported or non-scannable types.
claims.quote: Previously, file extensions were entered as free form text, which could result in unsupported or non-scannable extensions being used.

claims.claim: The roadmap attributes possible protection gaps to unsupported or non-scannable extensions.
claims.quote: This could lead to gaps in protection and increase processing overhead on endpoints.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes increased endpoint overhead from free-form extensions and reduced unnecessary processing from the curated list, without a numerical estimate.
claims.quote: This could lead to gaps in protection and increase processing overhead on endpoints. With the pre curated list, you can select only supported file extensions. This helps improve policy reliability and reduces unnecessary processing on endpoints.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence or meter specific to this curated-list change is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP pre curated file extension list license pricing meter disable picker PowerShell unsupported extensions'. Read Purview service description, Endpoint DLP getting-started, roadmap and MC1384415; no change-specific licence or meter found.

claims.claim: The Endpoint DLP getting-started page points to Microsoft 365 licensing guidance.
claims.quote: For information on licensing, see Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans; Microsoft 365 Service Descriptions

claims.claim: No prerequisites specific to the picker beyond Endpoint DLP licensing are stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP curated file extension picker disable tenant setting licensing meter supported extensions'. Read MC1384415, Endpoint DLP getting-started and policy reference; no additional picker prerequisite found.

claims.claim: File extension is scans content and permits Sensitive info type values in events or alerts.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP scans content for the File extension is condition, allowing you to see Sensitive info type values in events or alerts.

claims.claim: Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions does not scan file content.
claims.quote: In contrast, the Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions feature does not scan file content.

claims.claim: Events or alerts from the unsupported-file replacement do not contain Sensitive info type values.
claims.quote: you don't see values for Sensitive info type in events or alerts that are generated by policy matches.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-sharing-set-unsupported-files to sources for the statement about missing Sensitive info type values.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The unsupported-extension option does not support Device and device groups scoping in the policy location setting.
claims.quote: The Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions configuration option doesn't support scoping by Device and device groups in the policy location setting.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn marks the unsupported-files scenario as preview.
claims.quote: Apply controls to all unsupported files, is in preview.

claims.claim: Blocking extensions can break unallowed applications needing those files, with .dll, .json and .tmp given as examples.
claims.quote: certain apps might read or temporarily open files, like .dll, .json, .tmp during routine processes such as rendering, caching, or validating content. If you block these extensions, the app might fail to function properly

claims.claim: Unsupported file extension exclusions is a separate setting that narrows unsupported-files coverage.
claims.quote: Because this condition can potentially include many unsupported file extensions, refine detection by adding unsupported extensions to exclude.

claims.claim: No tenant UI or automation switch to retain free-form extension entry is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP curated file extension picker disable tenant setting licensing meter supported extensions'. Read endpoint settings, policy reference, New/Set-DlpComplianceRule and Set-PolicyConfig; no picker opt-out switch found.

claims.claim: The curated list cannot be switched off separately.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP curated file extension picker disable tenant setting licensing meter supported extensions'. MC1384415 removes free-form entry; policy reference, endpoint settings and PowerShell references publish no opt-out, but do not state a prohibition.
claims.fix: Replace 'No tenant setting for the picker is documented, so the curated list cannot be switched off separately.' with 'No tenant setting to switch off the picker is documented at the time of writing (November 2026).'

claims.claim: The printed Purview route through Policies, Enterprise applications & devices, Create policy, Custom and Custom policy leads toward the unsupported-extension action.
claims.quote: Open Data Loss Prevention > Policies. Select Enterprise applications & devices. Select Create policy and select the Custom from the Categories then Custom policy template from Regulations.
claims.fix: The cited route is correct but ends early. Extend it to 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Enterprise applications & devices > Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Full directory > Devices > rule > Conditions > Document could not be scanned > Actions > Audit or restrict activities on devices > Apply restrictions to specific activity > Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions'. The other Microsoft page https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-sharing-set-unsupported-files reverses Create policy and Enterprise applications & devices; note that documentation difference.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation sets Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions.
claims.quote: Searched: 'New-DlpComplianceRule Apply restrictions only unsupported file extensions EndpointDlpRestrictions', 'Set-DlpComplianceRule unsupported file extensions', 'Endpoint DLP unsupported PowerShell restrictions'. Read New/Set-DlpComplianceRule and Set-PolicyConfig; no setting found.

claims.claim: The roles needed to edit these policies are not stated in the sources read for the briefing.
claims.quote: This parameter requires membership in the Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.fix: Remove 'The roles needed to edit these policies are not stated in the sources read for this page.' The cited New-DlpComplianceRule reference specifies roles for EndpointDlpRestrictions, and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-deploy-policy publishes policy-creation permissions.

claims.claim: The roadmap and notice describe no change to roles, identities or permissions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) is improving how file extension conditions are configured

claims.claim: The notice does not describe changes to existing rules' block, warn or audit actions.
claims.quote: Existing policies continue to enforce as they do today unless edited.

claims.claim: The notice recommends reviewing current file extension lists before editing or creating policies.
claims.quote: If you plan to edit or create a policy: Review your current file extension list. Keep supported file extensions. Remove unsupported file extensions

claims.claim: Microsoft cautions administrators to test unsupported-file policies outside production.
claims.quote: Test this policy in a nonproduction environment before deploying it to your production environment.

claims.claim: Learn advises checking which applications interact with file types before implementing extension-based restrictions.
claims.quote: Before implementing extension-based restrictions, make sure you know which apps interact with these file types during standard operations

claims.claim: Learn about Endpoint data loss prevention provides monitored and unsupported file lists for comparison.
claims.quote: Monitored files; Unsupported File types: Endpoint DLP does not support monitoring for the following file types: .sys, .lib, .obj, .mui, .drv, .pf, .crdownload, .ini
